title: Bound-Conditioned Latent Inference for Progressive Image Compression
claim: Splitting each coding level into more bound-conditioned refinement steps yields progressively sparser, more efficient rate allocation at the same quantization precision.
layout: 2 image groups, 3×4 grid each, left-to-right arrow labeled LST
description: The figure shows two side-by-side heatmap grids, one for a rally car photo and one for a panda photo. Each grid has three rows labeled '1 step / plane', '2 steps / plane' and '4 steps / plane', under a vertical 'In-plane Auto-regression' label. The first column of the top row holds the original image. A black arrow labeled 'LST' above each grid points left to right and marks increasing trit-plane level. The cells are jet-colormap rate maps. Deep blue means low rate and red means high rate. Rate rises toward the right, with large red and yellow regions on object edges and textures. Moving down the rows, the maps become noticeably cooler and darker. This shows that more refinement steps lower the rate at the same plane. The eye goes first to the red top-right cells.
caption: Rate-allocation maps of the proposed bound-conditioned latent inference (BLI) codec. Each column corresponds to the same trit-plane level, i.e., the same degree of latent quantization, while each row uses a different number of in-plane refinement steps. The top row encodes an entire trit-plane in a single step, whereas the middle and bottom rows divide each trit-plane into two and four substeps, respectively. Colors indicate spatial rate allocation, with warmer colors corresponding to higher coding rates and cooler colors to lower rates. More frequent bound-conditioned updates iteratively refine the latent distribution within the same quantization level, yielding better rate efficiency without changing the final trit-plane precision.
abstract: Progressive image compression reconstructs images from prefixes of a single bitstream and therefore involves sequential latent inference under partial observations. Existing trit-plane codecs mainly treat decoded trits as discrete symbols for probability prediction, without fully exploiting their role as interval constraints on the underlying continuous latents. We propose bound-conditioned latent inference (BLI), a framework that reformulates progressive trit-plane coding as sequential latent inference under shrinking interval constraints. At each coding step, the trits decoded so far define lower and upper bounds for each latent element. BLI uses the center and width of these bounds, together with hyperprior information shared by the encoder and decoder, to jointly refine the Gaussian parameters $(Î¼,Ï)$ for entropy modeling and the latent estimate $\hat{y}$ for reconstruction. As additional trits are decoded, the feasible intervals shrink monotonically, yielding tighter constraints for the next inference step and enabling flexible in-plane refinement schedules. Experiments on Kodak, CLIC, and JPEG-AI show that BLI achieves state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance among progressive image codecs, reducing BD-rate by $17.78\%$ over DPICT and by $7.96\%$ over CTC on Kodak, while replacing CTC's plane-specific predictors with a shared model that uses about $5.3\times$ fewer parameters and achieves lower latency than CTC.
